title: Set a lintel across two free-standing posts without moving them
instruction: Lay the wooden lintel flat across the tops of the two standing posts, centred on them, and let go. Do not knock over or move either post.
context: Setting a beam or lintel onto supports that are not yet fixed (loose blocks, unbraced posts or temporary props) is a common step in building and in stacking work; a sideways bump or an off-centre drop topples or shifts a support and the load comes down. Each post here tips over under a sideways push of about 0.22 N (23 g-force) at its top, so the lintel has to be lowered straight down onto both tops at once.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, the midline is halfway between the arm bases (which are 61 cm apart), and heights are above the table top. Nothing is fixed to the table. Two posts (loose, pale unfinished hardwood, square section): each 40 x 40 mm and 110 mm tall, 125 g, standing upright on one end on the table, its sides square to the table edges, centred 25.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 7.0 cm left and 7.0 cm right of the midline (centres 140 mm apart, a 100 mm clear gap between their inner faces). Lintel (loose, darker stained oak): a box 220 mm long, 40 mm wide and 30 mm thick, 185 g, lying flat on a 40 x 220 mm face on the table with its long side parallel to the line through the arm bases, centred 18.0 cm in front of the arm bases and 20.0 cm right of the midline (on the right arm's side, 10.5 cm in from the right arm's base toward the midline). Laid centred across the posts, the lintel's ends overhang each post's outer face by 20 mm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state after the robot has let go, plus two quantities over the whole trial: how far each post's centre ever moved from where it started, in any direction, and how far each post ever turned from its starting pose, about any axis (a person reads both from the video and a tape on each post's taped footprint; a post lifted and put back, toppled and stood up again, or turned in place counts by its largest move or turn). This record starts when the scene is set to its starting layout; putting a post back on its mark during the trial does not clear it (in simulation it is cleared only when every object is within 0.5 mm of its start and at rest, reached in a single jump of over 20 mm in one control step, as a scene reset does and no push or carry can). At rest means moving less than 1 cm/s and turning less than 0.5 rad/s. The lintel is set when it lies flat (a 40 x 220 mm face down, within 5 degrees of level), at rest, with its underside within 1 mm of the top of each post (resting on it, not held above it), and the centre of each post's top face lies under the lintel (within its 40 x 220 mm outline). A post is upright when its axis is within 3 degrees of vertical and it is at rest. Centred: the lintel's two end overhangs past the posts (each measured along the lintel, from that end to the post under it) differ by at most 10 mm, and the centre of each post's top face is within 10 mm, sideways, of the lintel's centre line (so a centred lintel turned more than about 8 degrees from square to the posts is not centred). Score 1.0: the lintel set and centred, both posts upright, and neither post ever moved more than 10 mm or turned more than 15 degrees. Score 0.7: the lintel set but not centred, both posts upright, neither post ever moved more than 10 mm or turned more than 15 degrees. Score 0.5: the lintel set and both posts upright, no post ever turned more than 15 degrees, but a post moved more than 10 mm and at most 30 mm at some point. Score 0 in every other case: a post ever moved more than 30 mm or turned more than 15 degrees (including knocked over, lifted, dragged, swapped or turned in place), a post tilted more than 3 degrees or still moving at the end, or the lintel anywhere other than set on both posts (on the table, on one post only, on its 30 mm edge, tilted, still moving or held clear of the post tops). The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the condition at the last step.
reset_notes: Stand both posts upright on their taped footprints (40 x 40 mm squares centred 25.0 cm out, 7.0 cm either side of the midline) and lay the lintel back flat on its taped outline on the right arm's side. Nothing is consumed. Run with object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction, not measured from real wood; post ends are perfectly flat, so posts stand and tip exactly on their edges (real cut posts rock a little). No mortar, pad or fixing: the lintel is held by gravity and friction, as on dry-laid supports. Bench scale, far smaller and lighter than a real lintel. Lintel and posts have no marked top, front or grain; the lintel may lie on either 40 x 220 mm face, either way round.
